explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. The text says Israel entered the Wilderness of Sinai after leaving Rephidim, and camped there in front of the mountain (Exodus 19:2). Moses, Israel's leader, is about to do a LOT of walking up that mountain. Keep the name Sinai in your pocket, because it's going to matter.

Nice try, friend, but Paran isn't the name in this passage. The text says Israel set out from Rephidim and entered the Wilderness of Sinai, and camped there in front of the mountain (Exodus 19:2). That's a lot of desert names to juggle, and I'd mix them up too. Hold onto Sinai.
Zin isn't where this passage lands them. It says they "…entered the Wilderness of Sinai, and Israel camped there in front of the mountain." (Exodus 19:2) Sinai, friend, that's the one to remember.

The third month it is. The text says they came to the Wilderness of Sinai "…on the same day of the month that the Israelites had left the land of Egypt…" (Exodus 19:1) Same day of the month as the day they left. Now THAT is a date worth circling.

Seventh isn't the month the verse gives, friend. The text puts the arrival in the third month, on the same day of the month they left Egypt (Exodus 19:1). Third, not seventh. I'd have to check my calendar twice on that one.

Twelve months would be a whole year, and that's not what the verse says. It says "In the third month, on the same day of the month that the Israelites had left the land of Egypt, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai." (Exodus 19:1) Third month, same day of the month. Even the date is neat.

Eagles' wings, friend. The LORD says, "You have seen for yourselves what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself." (Exodus 19:4) It's a picture of being carried, and it ends with "to Myself." Not a bad ride.

A shepherd carrying someone is a lovely picture, but it isn't the one used here. The LORD says He carried them "…on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself." (Exodus 19:4) So the picture is wings, not arms. Keep the eagle in mind, friend.

A chariot would be fast, but that's not what the LORD says. He says He "…carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself." (Exodus 19:4) No wheels, no horses, just wings. And I've never seen a chariot with that kind of legroom anyway.
Possession is the word. The LORD says, "…you will be My treasured possession out of all the nations…" (Exodus 19:5) Treasured, friend. That's the kind of word you save for the good tray.

Servants isn't the word the LORD uses. He says that if they obey His voice and keep His covenant, "…you will be My treasured possession out of all the nations…" (Exodus 19:5) Treasured possession is what He offers. It's a big, warm word.

Guests sounds friendly, but the verse says something else. It says "…you will be My treasured possession out of all the nations…" (Exodus 19:5) Possession, friend, and a treasured one at that. Treasured is the kind of word you save for the last cookie in the box.
True! Right in the middle of His offer, the LORD says, "…for the whole earth is Mine." (Exodus 19:5) He's talking about all the nations and the whole earth. Every inch of it.

The text says the opposite of that. The LORD says that if Israel will indeed obey His voice and keep His covenant, they will be His treasured possession out of all the nations, "…for the whole earth is Mine." (Exodus 19:5) So yes, He says the whole earth is His. That's a big line to tuck inside an offer.

True, and they answer together. Moses had set the words before the elders (Exodus 19:7). Then all the people answered together, "We will do everything that the LORD has spoken." (Exodus 19:8) That's a big yes, friend.

The text says they answered with a yes. After Moses sets the words before the elders, all the people answer together, "We will do everything that the LORD has spoken." (Exodus 19:8) Then Moses brought their words back to the LORD.

explanations.answer: So the people hear Him speak with Moses
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the LORD gives. He says, "…I will come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you, and they will always put their trust in you." (Exodus 19:9) The people get to hear it for themselves. I like a plan where everybody gets to listen in.

explanations.answer: So the people can't see the mountaintop
explanations.explanation: The text never says anything about hiding the mountaintop. The reason the LORD gives is "…so that the people will hear when I speak with you…" (Exodus 19:9) The cloud comes so they hear Him speaking with Moses. Hearing, friend, not hiding.

explanations.answer: So their enemies can't find the camp
explanations.explanation: Enemies don't come up in this verse at all. The LORD says the cloud is "…so that the people will hear when I speak with you, and they will always put their trust in you." (Exodus 19:9) The point is the people hearing. I love a hiding-place idea, but that's not this one.

Clothes, friend. The LORD tells Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. They must wash their clothes" (Exodus 19:10) Clean clothes for the third day. I'd be rinsing my apron twice.
Tents would be a big laundry day, but the text doesn't ask for it. It says, "They must wash their clothes" (Exodus 19:10) Clothes, not tents. That's a lot less to hang on the line.
Feet are a fair guess after all that desert walking. But the verse says, "They must wash their clothes" (Exodus 19:10) Clothes are what the LORD names here. Feet are on their own.

explanations.answer: The LORD will come down on Mount Sinai
explanations.explanation: That's the big event. The LORD says, "…on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people." (Exodus 19:11) That's why they're washing clothes and getting prepared. When the LORD says be ready, you get ready.

explanations.answer: The camp will move on toward Canaan
explanations.explanation: Nothing in these verses says the camp is packing up. The reason for the third day is stated plainly: "…the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people." (Exodus 19:11) So the people are getting ready for Him to come down. The mountain is the story, friend.

explanations.answer: Moses will choose new leaders for Israel
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention new leaders at all. It says they must be prepared by the third day, "…for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people." (Exodus 19:11) The LORD coming down is the whole reason for getting ready.
Not quite, friend. The LORD's rule says, "Be careful not to go up on the mountain or touch its base." (Exodus 19:12) The base is off limits too, not just the climb. Staying back is the whole idea.

False, and the text is clear. The LORD says to tell the people, "Be careful not to go up on the mountain or touch its base. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death." (Exodus 19:12) So the base is off limits just like the slopes. No touching, friend, not even a little.

True, friend. After the punishment is laid out, the text adds, "…whether man or beast, he must not live." (Exodus 19:13) So the boundary around the mountain isn't only for people. Man or beast, the same rule applies. Even somebody's goat has to keep its hooves off.

The text says it does cover animals. After describing the punishment, it adds, "…whether man or beast, he must not live." (Exodus 19:13) So man or beast, the rule is the same. Even the goats have to hear about it.
The ram's horn, friend. The LORD says, "Only when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain." (Exodus 19:13) That long blast is the signal. Until then, you stay put.

A silver trumpet sounds fancy, but it isn't the one named here. The verse says, "Only when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain." (Exodus 19:13) It's a ram's horn, friend. Keep your ear out for that long blast.

Cymbals would make a lot of noise, but the verse doesn't mention them. It says, "Only when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain." (Exodus 19:13) The ram's horn is the signal. One long blast, then they may approach.

True. Moses consecrated the people and they washed their clothes (Exodus 19:14). Then he said to them, "Be prepared for the third day…" (Exodus 19:15) Clean clothes first, then the heads-up. That's a leader who thinks ahead.

The text says he did tell them. After the people washed their clothes (Exodus 19:14), Moses said to them, "Be prepared for the third day…" (Exodus 19:15) So that instruction comes right after the washing.
Thunder and lightning, friend. The text says, "On the third day, when morning came, there was thunder and lightning." (Exodus 19:16) And a thick cloud sat on the mountain too. Not a quiet morning.

Hail and rain aren't in this verse. It says, "…there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud was upon the mountain…" (Exodus 19:16) Thunder and lightning are what the text names. No umbrella needed, I guess.

The text doesn't mention a wind here. What it says is, "…there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud was upon the mountain…" (Exodus 19:16) So thunder and lightning are what broke out. Friend, that's plenty.
Trembled. The text says the horn blast went out "…so that all the people in the camp trembled." (Exodus 19:16) Everybody in the camp, not just a few. That's a blast you feel in your knees.

Cheering isn't what the text says. It says the thick cloud and the very loud ram's horn came "…so that all the people in the camp trembled." (Exodus 19:16) They trembled, friend. Cheering is a whole different mood.

Singing isn't the word the verse uses. It says the loud blast of the ram's horn went out "…so that all the people in the camp trembled." (Exodus 19:16) Trembling is the word, friend. I bet knees were knocking.

explanations.answer: The LORD descended on it in fire
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. The text says, "Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke, because the LORD had descended on it in fire." (Exodus 19:18) The smoke comes from the LORD coming down. I've had smoke in my bakery before, but that was just a forgotten batch, and all anybody did was open the windows.

explanations.answer: The people burned offerings on it
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that. Remember, the people were told not to go up on the mountain at all (Exodus 19:12). The reason given is that "…the LORD had descended on it in fire." (Exodus 19:18)

explanations.answer: Lightning set its trees on fire
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention trees or a lightning fire. It says, "Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke, because the LORD had descended on it in fire." (Exodus 19:18) So the cause is the LORD coming down. Not a brush fire, friend.
A furnace, friend. The text says, "…the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace…" (Exodus 19:18) I know furnace smoke. That's not a gentle puff.
A firepot isn't the comparison the text uses. It says, "…the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace…" (Exodus 19:18) A furnace is a much bigger picture. Think bigger than a pot, friend.

A campfire is a cozy picture, but it isn't the one the text uses. It says, "…the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace…" (Exodus 19:18) The comparison is a furnace, friend. Save the campfire for another night.

That's not what the verse says. It says, "…as the sound of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder." (Exodus 19:19) So God answers in the thunder, not in a gentle whisper. Thunder is the word the text uses, friend.

False, and good catch. The text says, "…as the sound of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder." (Exodus 19:19) God answered in the thunder, not in a whisper. That mountain was LOUD.

True, friend. The LORD has just called Moses to the summit, and Moses goes up (Exodus 19:20). Then the LORD says to him, "Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) Up the mountain, then right back down again. I bet his legs have opinions.

It does happen, friend. Once Moses has gone up, the LORD says to him, "Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) That's the instruction Moses gets at the summit. So True is the answer. Up the mountain, then straight back down with a warning.

Perish. The LORD says to warn the people "…not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) It's a serious word for a serious moment. The boundary is there for a reason.

Wander is much softer than what the text says. The LORD says, "…lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) Perish is the word, and I think it's the kind that makes you stand very still. Not a wandering matter, friend.

Stumble isn't the word here. The LORD says to warn the people "…not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) Perish, friend. That's a heavy word, and the text means it.

True. The LORD says, "Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them." (Exodus 19:22) The priests are named right there in His words. That little word "even" is doing real work.

The text says the opposite. The LORD says, "Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them." (Exodus 19:22) Even the priests, friend. The word "even" is doing real work there.

explanations.answer: The LORD already had them set a boundary
explanations.explanation: That's the reason Moses gives. He says to the LORD, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for You solemnly warned us, ‘Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’…" (Exodus 19:23) Moses is pointing back to what the LORD had already said. The boundary was the LORD's own instruction.

explanations.answer: The climb is far too steep for them
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say anything about the steepness. Moses says, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for You solemnly warned us, ‘Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’…" (Exodus 19:23) His reason is the LORD's own warning. Not a hiking problem, friend.

explanations.answer: The elders are guarding the only path
explanations.explanation: No guards are mentioned here. Moses' reason is, "…You solemnly warned us, ‘Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’…" (Exodus 19:23) The boundary came from the LORD's own words. Elders with clipboards aren't in the picture.

Aaron, friend. The LORD says, "Go down and bring Aaron with you." (Exodus 19:24) Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). The passage ends with Moses going down and speaking to the people (Exodus 19:25).

Joshua is a name you'll see in Israel's story, but he isn't the one named here. The LORD says, "Go down and bring Aaron with you." (Exodus 19:24) Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). Aaron's the one.
Hur isn't named in this passage. The LORD tells Moses, "Go down and bring Aaron with you." (Exodus 19:24) Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). So Aaron's the one the LORD names.
